title: Your brain can't ignore a word

probes.question: True or false: it takes longer to name the ink color of the word red printed in blue than the ink color of a neutral word.
The Stroop effect is named after whom?

image.alt: Illustration of four large colour discs, each with a clashing differently coloured disc in its centre

body.claim: Naming the font color of a word is slower and harder when the word spells a different color.
body.why: Say "blue" for the word red printed in blue ink and you take longer than for a neutral word. One explanation is the automation of reading: the mind automatically determines the semantic meaning of the word. It's called the Stroop effect, after John Ridley Stroop, who published it in English in 1935.
